clue.text: Bridge — one cad played, church official

parts.note: an arch is a bridge, or the curved span of one

indicators.note: the letters of one cad are played about with, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A bridge player complains that a rotter at the table cheated, with a cleric watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game; it is ARCH. 'played' rearranges ONE CAD into DEACON.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican cleric ranking just below a bishop, so a church official.

clue.text: Prepares to fight when invaded by marines

indicators.note: being invaded means having something come into the middle, so the word for when takes the marines inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A country gears up for war once marines land on its shores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invaded by' is a container signal: the marines go inside the word for when. RM is the usual crossword abbreviation for Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm is to equip with weapons, getting ready for battle; a verb in the third person matching 'Prepares'.

clue.text: Song lifted Solo, spy lacking inside

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters means reading them upwards, so backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words Solo, spy lacking

explanation.surface: A tune is pinched from a Han Solo spy story that is short of substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' takes OSPYLAC from 'sOLO SPY LACking' and 'lifted' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean style of song, originally from Trinidad, often with topical lyrics.

clue.text: Unsettling hint admitted in parts by disguised noble

indicators.note: unsettling the letters of hint disturbs their order
the rearranged letters are let into the word disguised in more than one place

explanation.surface: A nobleman in disguise drops a worrying hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettling' scrambles the hint, and 'admitted in parts by' means the scrambled letters go in at two separate places rather than as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished as an adjective means eminent, dignified and of high standing, which noble also conveys.

clue.text: A skill to cut delicate material according to taste

indicators.note: the word for skill cuts into the material, splitting it

parts.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
art can mean a skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is good at cutting fine fabric to suit the customer's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' is a container signal: the skill splits the fabric word. The French phrase is borrowed into English menus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from the menu item by item lets diners choose as their preference dictates rather than take a set meal.

clue.text: Sordid play seen off and on — or ignored in this way?

indicators.note: only every other letter is seen, alternately skipping and keeping, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A sleazy show is watched only intermittently, or perhaps not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen off and on' keeps the even letters of SORDID PLAY; the definition is a self-reference: the odd-numbered letters are the ones ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the letters in odd-numbered positions are the ones skipped, so they were ignored in an odd fashion, wittily turning the adverb literal.

clue.text: Spluttered: 'Hot and cold running over!'

indicators.note: over signals the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the hot and cold running fixtures over a sink are taps

explanation.surface: Someone splutters an exclamation about a bathroom with the water flowing over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TAPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spat is the past tense of spit, and spluttering means spitting out words or saliva in bursts.

clue.text: Egg on show, sandwiching in order

indicators.note: the word for show is split to hold the other piece between its halves like bread round a filling

parts.note: to prove is to show something to be true
OK means all right, in order

explanation.surface: A cook displays an egg tucked into a sandwich, arranged neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' looks like food beside 'sandwiching', but it is the verb in 'egg on'; 'sandwiching' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or goad them, and provoking is goading into action.

clue.text: Massive water rushes

parts.note: huge surges of sea, but rushes can also be read as reeds growing by water

explanation.surface: Great floods of sea pour in, or giant reeds at the water's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rushes' tempts as the plants of a riverbank; here it is the verb-turned-noun for surging floods.
explanation.definitionFit: These are enormous ocean surges, often caused by earthquakes, that rush onto the shore.

clue.text: This woman's bit of caramel is salty

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase caramel is salty is taken, the letters lying within it

explanation.surface: A woman offers a piece of salted caramel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes the name from caraMEL IS SAlty; 'This woman's' reads as 'This woman is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a female given name, so it can stand for a particular woman.

clue.text: 'Trouble and strife' should get album maybe — or daughter?

parts.note: an album is an example of a disc, a record
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A cockney's wife, 'trouble and strife', should receive a record or their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is cockney rhyming slang for wife, which the surface exploits, but here it is read literally as conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is disagreement and conflict between people, which trouble and strife literally describe.

clue.text: One wants to join another class and do something in the garden

definitions.text: One wants to join another class and do something in the garden

parts.words: One wants to join another class and do something in the garden
parts.note: a person aiming at a higher rank, also read as a friendly plant that grows up garden walls

explanation.surface: A pupil seeks to change classes and also take up gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half pictures a gregarious plant climbing in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving to rise into a higher social rank is said to climb socially; a climber is also a garden plant.

clue.text: Where most of us go at five to eleven?

definitions.text: Where most of us go at five to eleven?

parts.words: Where most of us go at five to eleven?
parts.note: five to eleven looks like a clock time but is the age range of pupils

explanation.surface: A question about where people head just before eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five to eleven' looks like 10:55; it is ages five to eleven, the years of British first schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain children attend the first stage of compulsory education between roughly ages five and eleven.

clue.text: Some rock and lead, say, have melted and tamely liquefied

indicators.note: melting changes the shape of the word have, so its letters are reworked
liquefying the word tamely likewise lets its letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Rocks and lead have been heated until they mildly turn to liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' and 'liquefied' together scramble HAVE and TAMELY. The definition covers both senses: loud rock music, and lead as an example of a dense metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a loud genre of rock music, and lead is an example of a dense, toxic element of that kind.

clue.text: The Spanish leading on opening stretch

indicators.note: the Spanish word goes first, leading what follows

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A Spanish runner leads at the start of a stretch of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' is an order signal: the Spanish article comes first. 'opening' looks like the start but is a noun, a gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to lengthen it, drawing it out further.

clue.text: Artist's following arrived, one holding pictures

indicators.note: following places the artist after the word for arrived, sending it second

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, meaning arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A painter's entourage turns up, one of them carrying artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's following' reads as 'artist is following', which puts the Royal Academician second; 'following' looks like a noun, an entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera stores photographs, so it is a device that holds images.

clue.text: One may be tall and long — stark even, occasionally

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: only now and then is a letter kept, every other one of the words stark even

explanation.surface: Someone tall pines starkly, even now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of STARK EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Conifers of this kind grow to great heights, so it is an example of something tall.

clue.text: Six-love, with nothing returned — one's played painfully at times

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: returned means the word for nothing is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A tennis set at six-love, with no return of serve, played in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This string instrument is bowed, and a beginner's scraping can be painful to hear.

clue.text: Wealthy upper-class fast to support surgeon's work

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting pieces sit underneath the first one

parts.note: an op is an operation, a surgeon's work
U is a label for upper-class usage
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A rich, posh patient pays a quick deposit for surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts U and LENT beneath OP in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly rich, showing great affluence.

clue.text: Naughty niece, imp wanting something for Christmas?

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is disorderly, so the letters of niece and imp misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A mischievous niece, a little devil, wants a Christmas present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges NIECE IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: These little pastries of dried fruit and spice are a traditional British festive treat.

clue.text: Show involving servant and soldier

parts.note: a page is a young servant or attendant
a soldier ant is a type of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A performance featuring a footman and an army man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' is a common crossword route to ANT, from the soldier caste of ants.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacular public show or procession, often with historical scenes.

clue.text: Tasty chops wife devoured with group

parts.note: chops is slang for the mouth or jaws
ate means devoured
a ring is a group, such as a gang

explanation.surface: Lamb chops that a wife wolfed down along with a crowd were delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chops' looks like cuts of meat; it is slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that makes the mouth water is appetising, so delicious-looking or tasty.

clue.text: Make confused commercial — not working, missing an intro

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: the word for not working loses its first letter, its introduction

parts.note: idle means not working

explanation.surface: An advert that has no opening and no point baffles viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing an intro' drops the first letter of IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle someone's brain is to muddle or befuddle it.

clue.text: Notices notices put up!

indicators.note: in a down clue putting the word up reads it from bottom to top, and it reads the same that way

parts.note: notices, as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone spots the bills being posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses SEES, which reads the same either way; the second 'notices' looks like a noun, as posters.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to spot or observe it, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Extremists on Twitter, wound up, went viral

indicators.note: the extremists are the end letters, the outermost ones, of the word Twitter

parts.note: to wind up is to finish, so wound up means ended

explanation.surface: Radicals online got worked up and their posts spread widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists on' takes T and R, the ends of TWITTER; 'wound up' looks like agitated but means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic trending on social media is rapidly gaining popularity, as viral content does.

clue.text: Tease about lack of youth and bony frame

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
C is short for circa, Latin for about
age is the opposite of youth

explanation.surface: Someone jokes about growing old and getting skinny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form a cage of bones protecting the chest, a skeletal framework.

clue.text: Instrument that makes money for the listener

indicators.note: what the listener hears is the word for money said out loud

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: A busker's instrument earns coins from those who hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the listener' signals the pun on LOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a plucked string instrument with a rounded body, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: A very quick shower?

parts.note: a speedy wash suggested, but it is a shower of shooting stars falling to earth

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a rapid wash in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like a wash; here it is a meteor shower, and the fragments travel fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks from space that survive the blaze through the atmosphere arrive at enormous speed, falling like rain.
